messages.subject: Handling of retries / replicated arrivals.
parts:
Hello,

I am looking for some inspiration to solve the following problem with Simmer in a somewhat efficient matter:

A predefined amount of arrivals exist, each with  an ID. Each ID ideally has a non fixed amount of entries (tries) each with different attributes corresponding to a temporal (this is a forward evolution, so absolute arrival times are increasing for each try within the ID) and spatial evolution.

Each arrival evaluates an acceptance function during the trajectory which is based on arrival attributes, resource attributes and current queue size, capacity size etc. If the function is accepted the trajectory goes forward and remaining arrivals tied to that ID should not be processed, or simply be rejected by some flag.
However if the acceptance function is rejected the next try tied to that ID should be allowed to be processed in the same manner. It is not a necessity that any try is accepted, so the individual "stop" condition is either an acceptance or running out of tries, i.e. every try being a leave / renege.

One line of enquiry was to clone arrivals on leave, renege etc. but as i undertand it's not possible to update the arrival time tied to the original data frame (i.e. essentially creating a delayed clone, and then having 1..n variables for each try in a single row in the initial data frame along with some try identifier to be updated).

The other idea is to seperate each try as a seperate arrival and then creating a giant global flagging variable outside the environment, which is to be updated once an acceptance has been made. Thus all subsequent tries will be denied. However with my limited knowledge this seems to create a lot of overhead, since we always have to evaluate every single arrival, leading to a worst case scenario.

Would appreciate any input / thoughts.

Best regards,
Christian

messages.subject: Re: [simmer-devel] Handling of retries / replicated arrivals.
parts:
Not sure if I fully understand what's the issue. But if you just need
retries, I would just rollback() after some delay.

Iñaki
